text:
Nadia B.: SI hit a blocker on an on‑prem Marketplace install. Installer fails pulling images because the customer's corporate proxy is doing TLS interception and causing cert errors.
Oliver P.: can you paste the exact error from the SI logs?
Nadia B.: SI log: ```Get \"https://registry.redwood.ai/v2/\": x509: certificate signed by unknown authority```
Samir V.: that indicates the proxy is resigning certs. Two pragmatic paths: 1) have customer add the proxy CA to node trust stores and container runtime trust (requires infra/SOC approval), or 2) use our signed offline bundle + import into their internal registry to avoid egress/TLS entirely.
security-bot: note: adding a custom CA to host trust is a security-sensitive change. Requires documented approval, timebox, and rollback steps.
Oliver P.: SI prefers the offline bundle route to avoid touching host CA. Link to signed bundle: https://artifacts.redwood.ai/offline-bundles/marketplace/v2.4.0-signed.tar.gz. We'll include a short checklist (checksum + gpg verify + podman/ctr import + push to mirror) and example Helm `values.yaml` to point to the mirror.
Nadia B.: I'll send the bundle + checklist to the SI and call out the proxy-CA option as a fallback with SOC template if they want to proceed later.
Samir V.: adding a runbook note: \"TLS‑intercepting proxies — prefer offline import; CA injection is fallback and must follow SOC approval template.\"
Nadia B.: SI will try the mirror import and update here. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
